title: Farmers rally in Brussels during EU leaders’ summit
location: Streets around the European Parliament, Brussels
participants_original: The Guardian reports hundreds of farmers from Belgium, the Netherlands and elsewhere; this is not a Belgium-only count. About 1,300 tractors/agricultural trucks is a vehicle count, not an attendee count.
threshold_50_evidence: The report directly says hundreds of farmers from Belgium, the Netherlands and elsewhere were present, supporting a 50+ gathering, while the exact Belgian participant count is not separable.

start_date.summary: The article reports the protest on Thursday 1 February 2024.

location.summary: Farmers blocked roads around the European Parliament in Brussels.

demands.summary: Taxes, costs and environmental rules; the report attributes EU-level calls to reform to farmers and describes the action as pressure on European leaders.

participants_original.summary: Hundreds from Belgium, the Netherlands and elsewhere; 1,300 tractors/trucks is vehicles, not persons.

protester_violence.summary: The article reports eggs, manure and fires; police hosed down burning straw/manure. It does not detail an assault on persons.

notes: A real public gathering and a 50+ cross-national crowd are supported. The known targets focus on EU institutions/leaders during an EU summit; Belgian participants and a Belgian prime minister in the city do not establish a demand to Belgium’s government. Keep home-state target unresolved. Distinct date from Jan31 convoy and Feb26 EU agriculture meeting; continuity is not assumed.
open_questions: Did any protesters explicitly direct demands to Belgium’s federal or regional government, separately from EU institutions?
What was the Belgian participant count within the mixed-nationality crowd?
When did the Brussels gathering physically end?
Were any people assaulted or was the main reported confrontation limited to objects/fire and police actions?
Was this a distinct event in the wider farmers’ protest wave or an episode continuation from Jan30–31?

title: Farmers rally near EU headquarters during agriculture ministers’ meeting
location: Brussels, near the cordoned-off EU ministers’ meeting area
organizer: Not established; a La Via Campesina representative is quoted, but the article does not state who organized the crowd.
participants_original: Reuters reports about 900 tractors jamming parts of Brussels; it does not give an attendee count. A protest crowd is described but number is not stated.
threshold_50_evidence: No person count is provided. Tractor count cannot establish the number of protesters. Eligibility remains pending_threshold and pending_state_target.

start_date.summary: Reuters dates the Brussels farmers’ rally to Monday, 26 February 2024.

location.summary: Farmers rallied outside the European Union headquarters near a cordoned-off ministers’ meeting area.

demands.summary: Low food prices, cheap imports and fair revenue were explicitly framed as demands of farmers toward the European Union.

participants_original.summary: About 900 tractors jammed parts of the capital; Reuters supplies no person attendance count.

protester_violence.summary: Reuters reports protesters throwing bottles and eggs; water cannon was used. No person injury is stated in this passage.

state_response.summary: Water cannon was used against protesters; public count of arrests or resulting dispersal not given.

notes: Protesters demanded action from the EU. Belgium’s agriculture minister attended the separate EU ministerial meeting and spoke about EU policy; this is not evidence that farmers targeted the Belgian government. Attendance and episode boundaries remain unresolved. Madrid and Poland actions in the same Reuters article are foreign-only and excluded from this unit.
open_questions: Is there evidence of a demand addressed to a Belgian federal or regional authority, distinct from the EU?
Did at least 50 people attend the Brussels rally, beyond the vehicle count?
What was the gathering’s physical end time and were any protesters dispersed?
Was the Feb26 action an episode continuation of the Feb1 EU summit protest, or a separate mobilization?
Did police detain or injure any attendees?
